title: Splitting a multilinear sum
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a set, let $\iota$ be an index set, let $s\subseteq\iota$ be finite, and choose $i\in\iota\setminus s$. Let $F$ assign a real coefficient to each finite subset of $\iota$, and let $X_j:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ for each $j\in\iota$. For every $\omega\in\Omega$, the sum over subsets of $s\cup\{i\}$ satisfies
\[\sum_{T\subseteq s\cup\{i\}}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)=\sum_{T\subseteq s}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)+X_i(\omega)\sum_{T\subseteq s}F(T\cup\{i\})\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega).\]
hypotheses_covered: $\iota$ is an index set with decidable equality
$F$ assigns real values to finite subsets of $\iota$
$X_j$ is a real-valued function on $\Omega$ for each $j\in\iota$
replaced: Let $s$ be a finite subset of an index set $I$, let $i\notin s$, let $F$ assign real coefficients to finite subsets of $I$, and let $X_j:\Omega\to\bbr$. For every $\omega\in\Omega$, $\sum_{T\subseteq s\cup\{i\}}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)=\sum_{T\subseteq s}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)+X_i(\omega)\sum_{T\subseteq s}F(T\cup\{i\})\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)$.
